samples.summary: Nothing tests that CliLoginConfirmMiddleware is actually wired onto GET /auth/github — the gate could be unwired and every suite stays green
samples.evidence: The confirmation page is the whole defense described in cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts (an attacker-navigated `?mode=cli&port=…` otherwise mints a code for the victim). Its unit spec (cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts) instantiates `new CliLoginConfirmMiddleware()` directly and never exercises the Nest route wiring; github-auth.guard.spec.ts only asserts the *fallback* when `__cliConfirmed` is absent (i.e. it passes whether or not the middleware is installed). Grep for `CliLoginConfirmMiddleware` and `AuthModule` shows only auth.module.ts, the middleware and its own spec; `packages/backend/test` contains no `/auth/github?mode=cli` e2e (only integration-helpers.ts mentioning the callback URL). So removing the `configure()` block or changing `forRoutes({ path: 'auth/github' })` breaks the CSRF gate with no failing test.

samples.summary: New `verifier` @Matches/@IsString validation on CliExchangeDto has no test; controller specs bypass validation entirely
samples.evidence: auth.controller.spec.ts calls `controller.cliExchange({ code, verifier })` with plain objects, so the ValidationPipe never runs and the `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43,128}$/` rule is never exercised (an empty or 500-char verifier would be accepted by the tests). Other DTOs in this repo do have dedicated validation specs (bigquery.dto.spec.ts, datasource.dto.spec.ts) that drive a real ValidationPipe, so the pattern exists and was not followed here.

samples.summary: `sheets import`'s new cell-table branch and the new `mode` response field have no command-level test — only the pure helpers are covered
samples.evidence: csv-parse.test.ts covers `isCellTable` and `buildCellMapFromTable` in isolation, but nothing drives the command: grep for `imported|mode` across packages/cli/test returns only login-command.test.ts (`mode=cli`) and a comment in csv-parse.test.ts. So the branch selection (`cellTable ? buildCellMapFromTable : buildCellMap`), the `mode: 'cells' | 'grid'` field now advertised in schema/registry.ts, and the `--start`-ignored behaviour could all be mis-wired without a failing test — unlike `sheets export --raw`, which did get a command-level test (test/sheets-export.test.ts).

samples.summary: After the state rewrite, the 'unknown/expired CLI state token' branch (BadRequestException) is no longer covered by any test
samples.evidence: The old spec test that exercised a non-CLI state (`falls back to web flow when state token is not CLI`) was deleted in this diff and replaced by web-flow tests that all pass a `web.`-prefixed state. No remaining test in auth.controller.spec.ts passes an arbitrary non-`web.` string (e.g. an expired CLI token) to `githubAuthCallback`, so the `throw new BadRequestException('CLI login state expired or invalid…')` path at auth.controller.ts:200 — now reachable for any state that fails `isWebOAuthState` — is untested.
searchedFor: Grep for 'state expired or invalid' in packages/backend

samples.summary: `loginErrorUrl`'s trailing-slash stripping and missing-FRONTEND_URL fallback are untested
samples.evidence: The spec's ConfigService mock always returns 'http://localhost:5173' (auth.controller.spec.ts:38), so the new `.replace(/\/+$/, '')` normalization and the `?? ''` fallback added at auth.controller.ts:299-301 are never exercised; a regression producing 'http://x//login?error=…' or '/login?error=…' would pass.

samples.summary: `renderConfirmPage`'s HTML escaping is never tested, and the page's CSP/Cache-Control/Referrer-Policy headers are unasserted
samples.evidence: cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts only asserts `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and reads the href params; no test passes a value containing `<`, `"` or `&` to `renderConfirmPage` (it is exported and takes arbitrary strings), so `escapeHtml` could be removed and the suite stays green. The `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'`, `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` headers set alongside X-Frame-Options are likewise unasserted.

samples.summary: `parseCliPort` has no direct boundary tests (1024, 65535, 65536, non-integer)
samples.evidence: github-auth.guard.spec.ts adds dedicated describes for `parseCliNonce` and `parseCliChallenge` but exercises `parseCliPort` only indirectly with '49152', '80' and 'not-a-port'; the upper bound (65535 accepted / 65536 rejected) and non-integer values like '1024.5' are untested.

finding.summary: Nothing tests that CliLoginConfirmMiddleware is actually wired onto GET /auth/github — the gate could be unwired and every suite stays green
finding.evidence: The confirmation page is the whole defense described in cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts (an attacker-navigated `?mode=cli&port=…` otherwise mints a code for the victim). Its unit spec (cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts) instantiates `new CliLoginConfirmMiddleware()` directly and never exercises the Nest route wiring; github-auth.guard.spec.ts only asserts the *fallback* when `__cliConfirmed` is absent (i.e. it passes whether or not the middleware is installed). Grep for `CliLoginConfirmMiddleware` and `AuthModule` shows only auth.module.ts, the middleware and its own spec; `packages/backend/test` contains no `/auth/github?mode=cli` e2e (only integration-helpers.ts mentioning the callback URL). So removing the `configure()` block or changing `forRoutes({ path: 'auth/github' })` breaks the CSRF gate with no failing test.

verdict.reason: The literal absence is real — no test exercises AuthModule.configure()/forRoutes (verified by repo-wide greps for mode=cli, auth/github, X-Frame-Options, renderConfirmPage, forRoutes/MiddlewareConsumer, and by reading all of packages/backend/test, whose AppModule e2e suites never request /auth/github). But the finding's blocking rationale is factually wrong: unwiring the middleware does NOT reopen the CSRF hole, because GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate mints CLI state only when req.__cliConfirmed is set (github-auth.guard.ts:72) and otherwise falls through to a cookie-bound web state (:80-84), so no code is ever minted for an unconfirmed ?mode=cli navigation. That fail-closed invariant is itself covered by a real, non-vacuous test (github-auth.guard.spec.ts:133-138: createState not called, __oauthState matches /^web\./). The new middleware behavior also has substantial real coverage in cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts (confirm/cookie match, single-use clearCookie, mismatch and no-cookie re-prompts, X-Frame-Options, __Host- prefix, param carry-through) with the real middleware instance, so this is not vacuous coverage or over-mocking. The residual gap is only that a mistyped route would break CLI login functionally with no failing test — coverage breadth (minor) under this lens's rubric, not "a clear behavior change with no meaningful test at all", hence not blocking.
